sources.README.md:
# ALTA AI Study Room

ALTA is an interactive Three.js study room. The Studio entry point is `index.html`, which loads the imported application in `design/ATLA/`. The imported code, 169-model manifest, models and six sound files remain there. The Dev Editor opens with **Ctrl + Shift + E**.

## Scripts

- `npm install` installs dependencies (lifecycle scripts are disabled by project policy).
- `npm run dev` starts the local preview server.
- `npm run build` creates the production build in `dist/`.
- `npm run preview` serves the production build locally.
- `npm run test` runs Vitest tests.

## Room controls

Click or tap the 3D door to enter or leave. Drag to orbit and use the mouse wheel or pinch to zoom; **Recenter Room** appears when the view moves away from the saved Full Room preset. Desktop hover uses a glow without labels. Plants and the desk surface are decorative. The chair focuses the desk. Clicking the cat only plays its reaction, with no popup.

**Coffee Mug** opens the Study Timer: tap 15m/25m/45m or a custom length, then Start/Pause/Reset; a gentle chime plays when time is up. **Wall Calendar** is an interactive monthly calendar — navigate months, tap any date to add study tasks or exam dates, with optional timed alarms. Chimes only play for a scheduled alarm and stop on **Dismiss**.

**Shelf** is master storage: upload local TXT, Markdown, PDF and image files (PNG/JPG/WebP with thumbnails), or add Google Drive/Docs/web links with a custom title. Diary notes and sketches saved this session appear here too. Click an item to **Open in Diary (Current Study)**, preview, or delete. The animated **Book** plays its open animation and opens the Current Study Diary — the active document, image or link plus all session notes, highlights and sketches, with **Save Session to Shelf**.

**Pen Cup** opens the Notes & Sketch Pad: freehand draw with mouse or touch (pen colors, eraser, clear), type or paste notes with 1-click Copy, then save to the Diary or archive permanently to the Shelf. The console and controllers open **Play Mode**, with scored multiple-choice and short typed questions generated locally from the active document, notes, or recent tutor topics.

A **?** button in the corner opens the one-card Quick Room Guide; it auto-shows only on your very first visit and is remembered in local storage. There is no background music. The speakers control alarm volume, room SFX and master mute. Click the chandelier for Lighting & Themes and **Save Lighting**.

The headset toggles browser voice recognition, subject to browser support, microphone permission and secure-context requirements. Recognized words are placed in the tutor draft. The right monitor opens the tutor, the left monitor opens Pomodoro, and the CPU toggles monitor power.

The supplied Desk, Shelf, Cat, Door and Full Room coordinates are built-in defaults. Saved Dev Editor camera presets and optional deployed scene configuration can override them. The desk surface itself is not interactive; its individual props are. Camera and orbit target are clamped inside the main study-room interior after OrbitControls updates during normal room use; the Door flow and open Dev Editor are exceptions.

## Assets and deployment

The Vite app uses source-managed model and audio imports and a relative base for subpath hosting. Draco decoding files are in `public/alta-draco/`; the production build emits an inventory used by the Dev Editor's project exporter. The full project exporter requires production build files; its development-server export endpoint is not yet provided. The external Puter service and fonts require an internet connection; local shelf and quiz processing do not send study material to Puter.

## Validation status

All 169 model files and six audio files are present and nonempty. GLB headers and embedded-resource references were checked statically, and all six audio files report a duration. Production build, browser decoding, sound playback, full export and interactive behavior still need verification in a runnable environment; these static checks do not prove the assets load successfully.
sources.GAME_DESIGN_DOCUMENT.md:
# ALTA AI Study Room — Game Design Document

## Overview

ALTA is an existing cozy, interactive 3D AI study room, adapted for Studio's Vite/Three.js project. The player enters the room, chooses a workspace, studies using the available tools and AI tutor, takes restorative breaks, and returns to focus. The existing product is the source of truth for features and content; this is an integration and targeted upgrade, not a redesign.

- Audience: people who want a relaxed, interactive study environment.
- Platform: web browser; 3D room with orbit camera and clickable objects.
- Pillars: cozy focus, useful study tools, approachable interaction, continuity of existing features.
- Progress: scored study quizzes and optional Pomodoro sessions; no unlock system.
- Cat interaction is ambient only: the 3D cat roams and reacts with a meow/purr on click, with no companion popup.

## World, Visuals, and Tone

- A furnished 3D study room with desk, monitors, posters, lighting themes, plants and a cat companion.
- Preserve existing models, interface styling, animations and cozy atmosphere. New effects should be subtle and support legibility.
- Indoor orbit camera stays inside the inner room bounds; Door preset transitions and the open Dev Editor are explicit exceptions.

## Existing Features and Controls to Preserve

- Start at the saved Door preset with no welcome modal. Click/tap the door from either side to open it, glide between Door and Full Room, and close it after arrival. Preserve saved presets and poster auto-focus.
- Cozy cat AI roaming and ambient reactions, with no companion popup.
- Lighting themes and settings; adjustable alarm chime and room SFX under a shared master mute.
- Dev Editor and its Ctrl + Shift + E shortcut, scene configuration and project export.
- Tutor/voice, notebook, the left monitor's Pomodoro and the coffee prop's break timer remain available.
- Existing pointer/orbit and interface controls remain intact.

## Requested Interaction Upgrades

- Shelf: master storage for local TXT, Markdown, PDF and image files (PNG/JPG/WebP with thumbnails), Google Drive/Docs/web links with custom titles, and archived diary notes/sketches. Items open in the Diary, preview, or delete.
- Book: play its embedded animation once per click and open the Current Study Diary — the active shelf item (document, image or link) plus session notes, highlights and sketches, with Save Session to Shelf.
- Pen Cup: Notes & Sketch Pad — freehand drawing with mouse or touch (pen color, eraser, clear), typed or pasted notes with 1-click Copy, and Save to Diary or Save to Shelf.
- Coffee Mug: Study Timer with 15/25/45-minute presets or custom minutes, Start/Pause/Reset, and a gentle chime when time is up.
- Wall Calendar: interactive monthly calendar; navigate months and tap any date to add study tasks, exam dates, or timed alarms. The chime runs only for an active alarm.
- Quick Room Guide: a corner **?** button opens a one-card object guide; it auto-shows only on the first visit and is remembered in local storage.
- Console and controllers: Play Mode creates scored local multiple-choice and rapid-fire fill-in-the-blank questions from the active document, notebook, or recent tutor topics.
- Plant pots: non-interactive decoration.
- Gaming chair: hover glow; click glides or snaps to the Desk view.
- Coffee stand and mug: hover glow; click starts, pauses or resumes the five-minute break, with reset in the toast.
- Wires: hover glow and a subtle pulse on click.
- Headset: toggle Web Speech API microphone input, with a glowing badge while listening; handle browser support and permission failures visibly.
- Speakers open the Audio & Speaker Station with alarm/SFX volume and master mute.
- CPU: toggle 3D monitor power between dark glass and powered-on standby glow.
- No continuous music or soundscape. The existing piano file is reserved for active reminders.
- Lighting popover: Save Lighting persists brightness, theme and color in localStorage for restoration.

## UI, Audio, and Accessibility

- The room props replace the top HUD on desktop and mobile. Only Recenter Room appears when the indoor view differs from Full Room. Desktop hover uses glow without floating labels; touch taps pick objects, while orbit and pinch do not activate them.
- Voice recognition depends on browser support, user permission and a secure context; indicate unsupported or denied states rather than implying the mic is listening.

## Scope, Assets, and Constraints

- Preserve existing ALTA source and features; use the Studio Vite/Three.js setup and retain the standard `dev`, `build`, and `preview` scripts and `dist/` build output.
- Imported source currently resides under `design/ATLA/`, including its manifest, models and sounds. The Studio starter currently has its own entry point under `src/`.
- User identifies 169 models and six audio files; counts and successful loading remain to be verified rather than assumed.
- Protect subpath deployment and avoid permanent references to scratch files. Scope stored settings to the project where practical without silently discarding existing user settings.
- Avoid feature rewrites or deletions; use existing interfaces and scene geometry when determining room boundaries.

## Validation and Milestones

1. Confirm open behavior questions, integrate the imported application and preserve its existing dependencies and asset paths.
2. Implement the requested camera, object, audio, microphone, monitor and lighting changes.
3. Validate production build, model and audio availability, asset paths, and existing-feature regression behavior. Runtime loading and interactive checks require a runnable preview or external environment.

## Current Implementation and Validation

- The Studio entry loads the imported ALTA app and source-managed models and audio, with local Draco decoders and an export inventory for production builds.
- Static inventory checked: all 169 unique manifest models and six audio files exist and are nonempty; GLB container headers and embedded-resource references passed static checks, and each audio file reports a duration. This does not verify browser decoding or actual playback.
- Build and interactive verification remain pending: the current editor mode cannot launch the app or run its build. Door transitions, camera geometry, microphone permissions, all interactions, audio playback and full exporter need a runnable preview.
- Supplied camera presets are fresh-load defaults; saved editor/deployed presets remain overrides. The desk surface is excluded from hover picking, but its individual props remain interactive. The clamp uses the main study-room interior after OrbitControls updates, except during the Door flow and editor use.
- Object-first entry, shelf, quiz, timer, calendar, sketch pad, diary, and guide changes require browser checks on both touch and desktop; text import, question generation, alarm-time and calendar-date calculations passed standalone checks. Image and clipboard code paths require a browser (FileReader/Clipboard) and remain unverified.
- The exporter references a development-only build endpoint that is not present in this starter; production export wiring has been added but remains unverified.
